
=================================================================
#97 The King for All  (676)
Arc: Silla-Tang War · place: surabol · tone: hard-won resolution
Logline: On the morning he becomes king of all Samhan, Munmu opens the hall to the yard. Five summers later, Kangrim asks him the question.
=================================================================
[0] ¶ **Bupmin**, **King Munmu** now, stands where a six-year-old once stole a sentence. The war is won, the ally has been shown the door, and the childhood dream has had the bad manners to come true.
[1] [MAP 676: Sixteen years, start to finish. Watch where the blue stops.]
[2] ── SCENE: The Collar ──
[3] ¶ It ends where it began: a woman in a room, getting someone else ready.
[4] ¶ Munhee is seventy. She is the last person alive who remembers all of it from the inside, and she is straightening her son's collar. She was twenty-six when this story started. Her sister burned a skirt on a hill so that she could be married.
[5] Munhee: Hold still. Your collar is crooked.
[6] King Munmu: Mother. Today I become king of all Samhan.
[7] Munhee: Then all the more reason to hold still.
[8] King Munmu: Mother. / I kept the childhood sentence.
[9] Munhee: I know. / I packed for every country that tried to stop you.
[10] ¶ She has been in the room for every single one of them. The sword was never in her hand, and she is the only one still standing.
[11] Munhee: Your sister rode out of this room to Daeya. / Hold still. I’m not losing another one to a door.
[12] ¶ A letter has come from Chang’an. It is the first in Inmun’s hand in twenty years, and it is very short.
[13] Kim Inmun: Brother. / The emperor made me King of Silla for a season. I got as far as the coast road before he changed his mind. I am told I abdicated. I agreed. / Word came that you said my name. I heard it. / — Inmun
[14] Munhee: His handwriting hasn’t improved.
[15] ¶ She folds it into his sleeve, next to his arm, where he will feel it all day.
[16] King Munmu: Father used to say a thing. A kingdom that lasts a thousand years.
[17] Munhee: He always did round the numbers up.
[18] ¶ Silla lasts nine hundred and ninety-two years. He was, as usual, very slightly optimistic and essentially correct.
[19] ── SCENE: The Hall ──
[20] ¶ The hall is full of bone. True Bone in the front rows, Head-rank Six behind them, and behind them the new men nobody has a rank for yet: Baekje captains who fought for Silla, Goguryeo’s guest king and his officers, a Mohe interpreter. Out in the yard stand the ones with no bone at all. They have come to see what a king for all looks like. Mostly he looks tired.
[21] King Munmu: Open the doors. / All of them. The yard too.
[22] ¶ The doors open. The yard comes up to the threshold and stops there, the way people stop at a river.
[23] King Munmu: Sixteen years of war were paid for with grain borrowed from people who had none. / Every grain debt from the war years is cancelled. Today. / The men of Baekje and Goguryeo who bled under our banners will hold Silla ranks. The same ranks.
[24] True Bone elder: Majesty. The bone ranks are older than the throne. If a Baekje captain sits where—
[25] King Munmu: When I was six I said everyone would have to listen to me. Even the bone people. / …I meant you, my lord.
[26] ¶ Somebody in the yard laughs. Then the whole yard does. The elder sits down. It is the first time that hall has ever heard the yard.
[27] King Munmu: I asked my uncle once. Every kingdom, or every person who bleeds for one. He never answered. / Both. Write that down.
[28] ── SCENE: The Eastern Star ──
[29] ¶ Thirty-four winters ago, three men looked up at one star and wanted the same title. One died a guest in Chang’an, still calling himself a king. One died in his bed, and the king of the dead came to fetch him in person. One left the title in his son’s mouth.
[30] ¶ That night the son climbs the hill above Surabol where two boys once lay on their backs, arguing about the sky.
[31] King Munmu: Uncle always said it was a planet.
[32] ¶ It sits among the stars without being one of them. He looks at it until the cold gets into his knees. Then he walks down to his own house, like anybody.
[33] ── SCENE: The Ancestral Temple ──
[34] ¶ In the morning he reports to his father. The tablet stands in the ancestral temple, and beside it hangs the iron oath from Mount Gain, the one he swore over his uncle’s horse.
[35] King Munmu: Father. I broke it. Every line. / Baekje is ours. Its prince is in Luoyang, with a title and no country. / His sons are growing. I asked. The gods have been lenient with us both.
[36] ¶ He leaves the oath where it hangs. The kings of Silla will have to walk past it every time they visit their fathers. He wants them to read it.
[37] ── SCENE: Five Summers Later ──
[38] ¶ Five summers later the king for all is dying, and he has left instructions his ministers do not like. No mound in the hills beside his fathers. Burn him, and put what is left in the sea the Wa come across.
[39] King Munmu: The war is over. Melt the swords. Make ploughs. / Lighten the tax at the markets and the ferries. / And don’t build me a tomb. The people would only have to carry the stones.
[40] ¶ Kangrim reads his name three times at the bedside — Bupmin. Bupmin. Bupmin. — the name the boy stole a sentence with, not the one the ledger writes.
[41] Kangrim: King Munmu. / Sixteen years of war, one hill, one ally shown the door, and a yard you let into the hall. / One question, then we walk. Were you a king of Silla — or a king for all?
[42] King Munmu: …Ask the ones with no bone. / There are more of them.
[43] Kangrim: The ledger has never asked them anything. / …I suppose I’ll start. Come. The sea is this way.
[44] ❝QUOTE (Samguk Yusa (三國遺事) bk. 2, Wonder 2 — King Munmu becomes a dragon; Ha & Mintz tr., p. 95): After I am gone I wish to become a great dragon that guards the country, to uphold the Buddha’s law and protect the realm.❞
[45] ¶ They burn him on the shore and put his bones under a rock a hundred paces out to sea, which is still there, and is the only royal tomb in the world with tides.
[46] ── SCENE: The Tablet ──
[47] ¶ Eleven years after the tide closes over him, an envoy comes from the Empress’s court with a complaint that is thirty years late. King Muyeol’s tablet in Silla’s ancestral temple says Taejong, and Taejong is the Second Emperor’s temple name, and a vassal may not share a name with the Son of Heaven. Nobody from the Empress’s court mentions the iron oath hanging beside the tablet, broken in every line.
[48] Tang envoy: Your late king has borrowed a name that belongs to the Second Emperor. / Change it.
[49] ¶ Munmu’s son answers in writing.
[50] Silla reply: Our late king had a great deal of virtue. While he lived he had a good minister, Kim Yushin, and the two of them were of one mind, and they made the three Han one. / We thought that was worth a name. We did not know it was already taken.
[51] ¶ The court reads the name Kim Yushin, and an old archivist goes looking. He finds a note in the late emperor’s own hand, from his boyhood: a voice in the sky once told him that one of the Thirty-Three Heavens had been born in the east as a general. Nobody ever learned whose voice it was. Heaven gossips more than it lets on. The complaint is dropped. The tablet still says Taejong.
[52] ¶ **But we left someone in the snow. The winter Pyongyang fell, a Mohe father walked north with something in his pack…!**
